summary: St. Joe NF 20-foot pole tower with L-4 cab built 1932 in Shoshone County; 1934 wildfire came within a mile; destroyed 1956.

facts.design: 20-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab
facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1956 per all three lookout pages. No source describes what remains at the site.

visit.trail_note: The Idaho Fire Lookouts page lists the site as a hike-in, marked destroyed. No source describes access to the site now.

events.note: 20-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab, per all three lookout pages.
A wildfire came within about a mile of the station at midnight on August 23, 1934. The Morning Oregonian account, quoted on the Idaho index, does not name the fire.
Destroyed in 1956 per all three pages; the cause and the exact date are not given.

evidence.supports: built 1932 as a 20-foot L-4 tower; destroyed 1956

evidence.supports: L-4 is a standard 14 by 14 foot pre-cut frame lookout house, built 1929 to 1953
evidence.quote: The L-4, also known as an "Aladdin", is a standard 14 x 14 foot frame pre-cut lookout house built from 1929 through 1953.

the account is attributed to the Morning Oregonian

sources.title: Lookout Styles of the Nez Perce National Forest

notes_for_editor: The three lookout pages agree on the 1932 tower and the 1956 loss, but none gives a cause, a day, or site conditions. The 1934 fire is not named in the quoted account. The L-4 description comes from a Nez Perce NF style guide and is general, not specific to this site. The index's (Kresek) attributions were not traced. Brief height 6.1 m matches the 20 ft figure.
